writeup.headline: Fortinet rates Buy on strong growth, margins and net cash, held back by a high valuation.
writeup.thesis: Fortinet scores 73, a Buy, because its business numbers are strong across the board. Growth scores 78, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 25.6% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 18.8%, and growth sped up by 5.5 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 95 on an 80.2% gross margin, a 32.4% operating margin and a 41.4% FCF margin, with diluted share count down 4.2% year on year, and the balance sheet scores 100 thanks to net cash. Trend (87) and news (71) also help: the shares are up 106.3% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and the company raised its FY2026 revenue and billings guidance for the third time this year. The main drag is valuation at 21: multiples are high in absolute terms (17.0x sales, 41.0x FCF, 50.8x EV/EBIT, with the FCF yield 2.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), and the stock is expensive against its own history.
key_risks: High absolute multiples (17.0x sales, 41.0x FCF) leave little room if growth slows; P/S is more expensive than at 54 of the last 61 month-ends.
Slower service revenue growth weighed on the reaction to Q3 results and could weigh on future quarters.
Critical security vulnerabilities, including an actively exploited FortiMail zero-day, could hurt customer trust.
After a large run-up, the price is 10.6% below its 52-week high, and a broader pullback could hit the trend score.
Arete Research cut the stock from Buy to Sell, a sign of mixed analyst views.
what_would_change: A 7-point rise in the score to 80 would lift it to Strong Buy, for example through a less expensive valuation after a pullback, or further growth acceleration.
A 9-point drop to below 65 would cut it to Hold, for example if growth slows and the trend score fades.
Weaker news, such as negative post-earnings analyst actions or legal fallout from security flaws, would pull the news score down from 71.
